Procedures for route planning on the job
Trainers ask staff to read this twice, and by the end of this page you will know why

This page matters because route planning shapes the comfort, safety, and calm of every companion animal entrusted to Aurelia Skyways. If the route is chosen carelessly, a pet may face avoidable stress, and the traveler may receive poor guidance from our desk. As a new member of the Companion Animal Travel Desk, you must learn to read the journey as a whole, not as a set of isolated steps.

Begin by confirming the animal's needs, the type of carrier, and the points at which handover will occur. Then compare the route options with the service notes, the acceptance rules, and the spaces available for transfer. Speak plainly, but never loosely. A careful explanation reassures the traveler and prevents later confusion.

When a traveler brings a cat, check the carrier first and make sure the accepted size is followed exactly. <<FACT F067>> After that, verify that the carrier can be handled easily through check-in and boarding without strain to staff or delay to the animal. Use the same disciplined method for all cases, because a minor oversight may become a serious problem once the journey begins.

For birds, the certificate must be reviewed with equal care. <<FACT F083>> If the document is missing, unclear, or out of sequence with the rest of the record, pause the booking review and direct the traveler to the proper support path before any route is confirmed. Do not rush this step. It is kinder to correct an error early than to discover it at the gate.

You should also note whether the traveler is moving with more than one pet, whether the pet will remain in the cabin or travel separately, and whether a welcome team handoff will be required before boarding. Use calm language, take accurate notes, and keep the record aligned with the itinerary. If the pet is anxious, advise the traveler in a steady and respectful manner.

What to remember is simple: plan the route with care, verify the documents, and protect the animal's welfare at every stage.
